display.title: Episode 174: The Missing Wallet (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: During Sefirah, Uncle Yossi teaches that time is precious, with the parable of the lost nickel, and tells how a poor boy who returned a lost wallet was richly rewarded.
display.summary_long: In the middle of Sefiras HaOmer, Uncle Yossi explains one lesson of counting the days: time marches on and cannot be stopped, but we control what we fill it with. A lost day cannot be brought back, as in the story of Zalman, who keeps asking his father to replace a nickel that fell through a hole in his pocket, until he learns to forget the lost nickel and guard the ones he still has. So we make every day count with davening, Torah and mitzvos. After a sponsor message, a class from a Brooklyn girls' school leads the Shema. Story time, about honesty in preparation for receiving the Torah, tells 'The Missing Wallet'. Dovid, a twelve-year-old orphan, leaves school to sell newspapers when his widowed mother falls ill, and the superintendent warns that they will be evicted. Dovid finds a wallet full of thousand-dollar bills, and his mother insists they find its owner, a banker. The grateful banker presses a reward on him, and on a second visit learns that Dovid's late father was his childhood friend who once lent him the money to come to America. He makes them partners in his fortune, and Dovid returns to yeshiva.
display.lesson: Make every day count, because lost time never returns; and be honest, for Hashem richly rewards honesty.

date.note: 'Right in the middle of the days of Sefirah' (9 Iyar = day 24) and no mention of Lag BaOmer; four weeks after ep. 170 (2 Apr 1985). Weekly estimate (21 May) is 3 weeks late.

advisories.note: A fatherless boy leaves school to support his sick, impoverished mother, and they are threatened with eviction.
The boy's mother is bedridden for months.
